gap_rows.title: rwb-integration booking confirmation (deployment slice): the login and secret reference, the JOB-08 ownership, the alert thresholds, the runbook ownership and the backfill limit are not fixed by a source
gap_rows.source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42, 43, 44 and 45; Ownership Map tables job_catalog (P2) and API rows POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (owner P1) and GET /admin/scheduled-jobs (owner P2); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (job_catalog) and Appendix T-A (API-P2-009); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16 and 27; FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 5 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.7, R7.2 s12 and R9
gap_rows.section: 3 Preconditions, 10 Authority, 11 Data, 12.5 to 12.7, 13 Solution plan, 14 Validation and messages
gap_rows.description: One combined row for the deployment slice of this key. (1) Identity: no source names the login, the secret reference or the worker identity of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the release must carry one login and one task queue. (2) Job ownership: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08 and slides 42 and 43 do not list rwb-integration among the consumers of AceDataReady and TreatmentApproved, while this realignment registers the workflow on the rwb-integration queue; the release registers it there and records the conflict. (3) Schedule absence: JOB-08 is event-started, so the release creates no Schedule and the catch-up and overlap semantics of a Schedule do not apply; no source states the run window that replaces them, so the late-batch alert threshold carries it. (4) Alert thresholds and series definitions: no source fixes the four thresholds, the aggregation window of the four series or the dimensions, and they are values of the environment. (5) Runbook: no source names the four runbook entries, their owner roles or their review cycle. (6) Backfill: no source fixes the backfill limit per run or the reuse window of the Idempotency-Key. (7) Message text: MSG-P1-001 has two wordings and FSD P2 Integration v3 gives the current one; the other four alert texts are the legacy texts unchanged. (8) Build ID: no source fixes the build ID format or the worker versioning policy of this release.
gap_rows.evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 13 fixes no deployment value and names no identity; TSD P2 Integration v3 API-P2-009 reads the job catalogue with owner, schedule, run book and alert threshold but names no booking-confirmation row; Architecture v5 slide 44 puts JOB-08 with rwb-payment; the Ownership Map gives job_catalog to P2 and keeps the generic rerun with P1; no source fixes the run window, the four thresholds, the four runbook entries or the backfill limit of this run.
gap_rows.owner_role: DevOps engineer; platform administrator; platform workflow kit owner; business on-call owner for the package alerts
gap_rows.proposed: Fix the identity, the secret reference and the probe checks in RWB-P2-E2007-OPS; register the workflow on rwb-integration and record the JOB-08 owner conflict; take the four thresholds, the series windows and the backfill limit as values of the environment; write the JOB-08 job catalogue row with its run book path; and review the four runbook entries with the on-call rota.

asm_rows.text: The release registers BookingMatchWorkflow and its six activities on the rwb-integration task queue in namespace rwb-recovery as an event-started workflow of AceDataReady, creates no Schedule for JOB-08, and records the Architecture v5 slide 44 owner row of rwb-payment as superseded for this job.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08 and slides 42 and 43 list no rwb-integration consumer row, while the accepted split of this legacy key registers the workflow here; a release that shipped either reading silently would leave the run unstarted or doubled.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; RWB-P2-E2007-APP section 12.6.
asm_rows.applied_in: 1 Story, 4 Flow, 8 BR3, 12.5, 12.6 and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect; platform workflow kit owner; the rwb-payment owner
asm_rows.impact: The registration check asserts the queue, the seven registrations and the event start, and asserts that no Schedule exists.

asm_rows.text: The four alert thresholds, the aggregation window of the four dashboard series and the run-window expectation that triggers the late-batch alert are values of the environment and are reviewed with the business on-call owner, not fixed in code, a chart template or a document.
asm_rows.why: No source fixes any threshold, window or dimension of this run, and the legacy story only names the measure REC-03 and the two task messages.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 2, 5 and 16; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 42; ADR-023; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17.
asm_rows.applied_in: 11 Data, 13 Solution plan and 14 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
asm_rows.confirm: Business on-call owner (RW-COE) and the observability owner (RWB-PLT-OBS)
asm_rows.impact: Each environment tunes its own thresholds; the alert rules, the message IDs and the runbook links do not change.

asm_rows.text: The four runbook entries — event not received or worker not polling, missing-booking wave, terms wave, and no package in force with a late ACE batch — are owned by the DevOps team for the platform steps and by the business on-call owner for the package steps, and are reviewed by the on-call rota before promotion.
asm_rows.why: No source names the runbook entries, their owners or their review cycle, and an alert without an owned entry is not operable.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 5, 10 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; ADR-023; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s14.
asm_rows.applied_in: 10 Authority, 11 Data, 13 Solution plan and 15 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
asm_rows.impact: Each alert links one owned entry, and the runbook review is a promotion gate rather than a post-release task.

asm_rows.text: The release carries the rwb-integration login as a secret reference from the platform secret store, polls the rwb-integration task queue only and requests no grant on recovery or on another rwb_* schema.
asm_rows.why: No source names the login, the secret reference or the worker identity of rwb-integration under DP-02, while the platform rules require one login per service and one task queue per service.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02 and DP-10; Ownership Map schema row rwb_integration; legacy RWB-E2-007 section 10.
asm_rows.confirm: ACE team and DBA (RWB-PLT-DB); platform administrator
asm_rows.impact: The release is provisioned once the login is allocated; the readiness probe names the first successful authorise call as its dependency check.

asm_rows.text: The build ID is the one the workflow kit supplies for the release commit, worker versioning is enabled so a new build takes new runs while the old build drains, and the payload codec is attached to every client and worker of the deployment.
asm_rows.why: No source fixes the build ID format or the versioning policy, while the workflow kit requires both for a workflow that runs unattended on an event.
asm_rows.read: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 24.
asm_rows.impact: An in-flight run finishes on the build that started it, and a rollback redeploys the previous chart with its own build ID.

asm_rows.text: The backfill limit per run and the reuse window of the Idempotency-Key are values of the environment; a date already completed under the same key replays the stored answer, and a treatment that failed on a consumed contract is picked up by the next business date rather than repaired by a script.
asm_rows.why: No source fixes the backfill limit or the key window, while the legacy repeat-run rule (one record and one open task per treatment and date) has to hold for a backfill as well as for an event-started run.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4 and 5 (X5, X6); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09; RWB-P2-E2007-CON section 12.1.
asm_rows.applied_in: 5 Exception paths, 8 BR6, 11 Data and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
asm_rows.confirm: DevOps team; platform workflow kit owner; the rwb-integration owner
asm_rows.impact: The backfill is safe to repeat and needs no repair script; both values are tuned per environment.

asm_rows.text: MSG-P1-001 uses the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording in the late-batch alert and in the skipped-run message, and the other alert texts are the legacy and platform texts unchanged.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story and the current FSD give different wordings for MSG-P1-001, and an alert must carry the text the catalogue holds.
asm_rows.read: FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E2-007 section 14; Template and Rules v1 R3 and R7.3.
asm_rows.confirm: Platform message catalogue owner; business analyst of P2
